source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration — Memory Reference Code (MRC) Promote Warnings = Disable — Promote Warnings = Disable • If promotion knobs are enabled then BIOS will not disable the DIMMs on the channel and continue booting as mentioned previously but will instead consider the bad PMIC as a fatal error and hang the system. • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory DFX Configuration — Power Management Integrated Circuit (PMIC) Failure Isolation = Enable — PMIC Secure Mode = Disable • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Verify that the target PMIC has no history of errors or currently logged errors. Following values should all be zero. >>> ras.mem.PMICErrorStatus(socket=0, mc=0, channel=0, slot=0) 3. Inject a "Critical Temperature Shutdown" on the target PMIC by writing 0x82 to register 0x35. Python exception print statements are expected with the CScripts version used and were omitted from the logs below. PMIC behavior is not uniform across all PMICs so the CScripts command below should check the PMIC vendor ID and revision for known problematic PMICs. >>> ei.mem.injectPMICError(socket=0, mc=0, channel=0, slot=0, raw_value=0x82, verbose=True) 4. At this point, the system has shut off. AC power cycle the system and analyze the BIOS serial log as described in the follow steps. 5. As seen in the BIOS serial log, BIOS found PMIC register 0x05 to be non-zero and 0x3 means it was a "Critical Temperature" error. An EWL of type 1 is logged with a major/minor warning code of 0x46/0x5 which decodes to WARN_POWER_FAILURE/WARN_DDR5_POWER_FAILURE CRIT_TEMP. 6. Also shown in the BIOS serial log, note that further EWLs of type 1 were logged for each rank on the target channel since they're all disabled. The major/minor warning code of 0xA/0x3 decodes to WARN_USER_DIMM_DISABLE/ WARN_USER_DIMM_DISABLE_RANK_DISABLED. 7. Also note that the active memory has been reduced since the two 64GB DIMMs on socket 0 channel 0 have been disabled. 8. The system should successfully boot. 9. Check the target DIMMs PMIC registers and confirm that register 0x4 is equal to 0x10 indicating that this PMIC has saved the critical temperature event to its error log history. Also confirm that register 0x5's PMIC_ERR_LOG bitfield indicates that there was a critical temperature event. >>> ras.mem.PMICErrorStatus(socket=0, mc=0, channel=0, slot=0) 10. To bring the system back to a good working state it's recommended to clear the target DIMMs PMIC error registers by doing the following command and then reflashing the IFWI or clearing CMOS since otherwise BIOS will track the disabled DIMMs on subsequent boots and continue to disable them. >>> ras.mem.clearPMICErrorStatus(socket=0, mc=0, channel=0, slot=0, verbose=True)

disposition_reason: Raw0x82 is meant to latch a critical-temperature shutdown in the target PMIC, so the immediate power loss is only the stimulus. The actual isolation behavior is established after AC restart: BIOS must decode register0x05, emit the critical power warning, disable every rank on the target channel and boot with the corresponding capacity loss. Registers0x4/0x5 prove persistence rather than a transient shutdown. Because BIOS remembers disabled DIMMs, clearing only the PMIC register is insufficient; the approved IFWI/CMOS reset and restored full inventory close the test safely. test_case.test_name: PMIC Failure Isolation — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Validate that BIOS isolates a channel after a DDR5 PMIC critical-temperature shutdown, logs the exact power/rank-disable warnings, boots with reduced memory, retains the PMIC event history and can be returned to a fully healthy state.
required_package: GNR/BIOS/BMC/IFWI/OS versions and socket0/MC0/ch0/slot0 DIMM/PMIC PN, vendor ID and revision
CScripts version/hash/license and raw0x82 support matrix including known exceptions
Approved promotion/isolation/secure-mode/POR settings and expected two64GB isolation scope
Controlled AC-cycle owner/path, POST/boot deadlines and serial/BMC capture
PMIC clear semantics, signed compatible IFWI or exact CMOS-clear recovery and full-memory acceptance
test_case.test_command: Capture platform/DIMM/PMIC identity, settings, logs and capacity; verify all PMIC status fields zero; inject approved raw0x82 to target PMIC and capture shutdown; perform one controlled AC cycle; analyze serial EWL0x46/0x5 and per-rank0xA/0x3, confirm two64GB DIMMs disabled and successful reduced-memory boot; read PMIC reg0x4=0x10 and reg0x5 critical-temp bit; preserve evidence, clear target status once and perform approved IFWI reflash or CMOS clear; verify full memory and health restored.
test_case.expected_result: Error is injected successfully. Error logs should match.

safety_gate: Dedicated workload-free SUT with stable OOB/serial and recoverable firmware
Do not clear baseline logs; reject nonzero unexplained PMIC status or unsupported vendor/revision
Inject once and expect power loss; no automatic restart/retry
Stop on unexpected EWL, wrong DIMM isolation, failure to boot or unsafe reduced-memory state
Clear/reflash/CMOS only after evidence preservation and explicit owner approval; verify full topology restored
expected_evidence: Platform/DIMM/PMIC identity, source settings, preexisting-log snapshot, zero PMIC baseline and full capacity
Raw injector output, shutdown and controlled AC-cycle timestamps
Complete BIOS serial with EWL0x46/0x5 and per-rank0xA/0x3
Disabled target ranks/DIMMs, exact active-memory reduction and successful boot
PMIC reg0x4=0x10 and reg0x5 critical-temperature history
Clear command plus IFWI/CMOS recovery, restored settings/full memory and final OS/BMC health
test_case.recovery: Reference EDKII paths and non-POR setting require project mapping/approval. Promotion knobs must remain disabled because enabling them changes expected fatal/hang behavior. PMIC Secure Mode disablement is security-sensitive and must be restored.
